content.text: Balaia and Pine Cliffs aren't sibling courses at the same resort — they're two completely separate clubs that happen to sit a few minutes apart near Albufeira, and both get recommended for the same reason: a proper round in under two hours. Beyond that, they're not really alternatives to each other. Here's who each one actually suits.
Two different resorts, two different kinds of short round

Balaia is a budget, no-frills par-3 course attached to a 4-star holiday village. Pine Cliffs is a nine-hole course built into the grounds of a 5-star Marriott Luxury Collection resort, with one of the most photographed golf holes in Portugal. Both take roughly the same time to play — but one is designed to remove pressure, and the other is designed to give you a story to tell.

Every one of Balaia's nine holes is a par 3, running from 67 to 160 metres from the yellow tees, which makes it one of the genuinely easiest ways to get a beginner or a junior onto a real golf course. It opened in 2001 and sits inside the Balaia Golf Village estate, with a 40-bay driving range and golf academy on site if you want to work on your swing first. A day's golf costs visitors **€50** on the club's 2025-26 price list, among the cheapest rounds in the Algarve.
Stay right on the course at the [Balaia Golf Village Resort](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/balaia-golf-village.html).
Pine Cliffs: the bucket-list clifftop hole

Pine Cliffs plays nine holes to a par of 33, perched on sandstone cliffs above Olhos de Água. Martin Hawtree designed it, and it's built around the sixth, the **Devil's Parlour**: a 197-metre par 3 played from 60 metres above the Atlantic, over a ravine, to a green on the cliff edge. It's genuinely playable for beginners thanks to the short holes, but that one tee shot is not for the faint-hearted. Nine holes cost visitors from **€59** on the club's 2026/27 price list.
The course sits inside the resort, with the [Pine Cliffs Residence](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/pine-cliffs-residence.html) right on site.

If you're introducing a beginner to golf, playing with juniors, or just want a relaxed, cheap round with zero pressure, play Balaia. If you want the photo, the resort experience, and one genuinely thrilling tee shot over the ocean — even if the rest of the round is gentler than it looks — play Pine Cliffs. Neither replaces a full 18-hole day out; both are exactly what they're built to be: a good two hours of golf that doesn't ask much of your schedule.
